Not everyone knows this (and I won't pretend I did), but Apple has actually published extremely detailed dimensional drawings for dozens of their devices to help accessory manufacturers design compatible products. Here are the details.

Apple hardware, drawn in extreme detail

For nearly 30 years, Jason Kottke has been one of my primary sources for interesting content on the internet (and beyond), and there's so much I'd never have discovered without him.

A few days ago, he published this post linking to the "Dimensional Drawings" section of the Apple developer site's accessories area.

In short, it's a collection of incredibly detailed technical drawings, currently covering 96 devices in total, including the newly released iPhone 18 Pro, Apple Watch Ultra 4 and Series 12, as well as AirPods 5.

The list also includes products like MacBook Neo and Siri Remote, as well as AirTag, AirPods charging cases, and even ZEISS optical insert accessories for Apple Vision Pro.

Each document contains precise measurements ranging from overall device dimensions and curvature, to buttons, cameras, sensors, speakers and connection ports, along with detailed "keepout zones" indicating where certain materials cannot be placed.

Although these documents are primarily intended for accessory manufacturers, they should also be quite appealing to anyone with even a passing interest in hardware or industrial design, or who simply appreciates Apple's meticulous attention to detail.

To view Apple's dimensional drawings, click this link. If you haven't yet followed kottke.org, be sure to start following it.
